title: Cap. IV Arg. 6: perpetual use of Electi — in salvation contexts always means believers
pass_a_gloss: Argument 6. Another argument is sought from the perpetual use of the word Elect, as often as it is placed with respect to salvation; as Rom. 8. Who will accuse against God's elect? and Rom. 11. The elect have obtained, and Matt. 22. Many called, few elect. From these and other like places they argue thus; The word of the Elect, when it is treated concerning salvation, is perpetually used in the Scriptures for believers: Therefore there is no election to salvation except of believers.
pass_b_english: Arg. 6. Another argument from the standing use of Elect wherever salvation is in view — Rom. 8: Who will accuse God's elect?; Rom. 11: The elect have obtained; Matt. 22: Many called, few elect. From these and like places: the word Elect, when Scripture speaks of salvation, is always used for believers; therefore there is no election to salvation except of believers.
source_text: Arg. 6. Petitur aliud argumentum a perpetuo usu vocis, Electi, quotiescunque ponitur cum respectu ad salutem; ut Rom. viii. Quis accusabit adversus electos Dei? et Rom. xi. Electi assecuti sunt, et Matth. xxii. Multi vocati, pauci electi. Ex hisce aliisque locis consimilibus ita argumentantur; Vox Electorum, cum de salute agitur, perpetuo in Scripturis usurpatur pro credentibus: Ergo nulla est electio ad salutem nisi credentium.
